doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Dr. Morton-Finney and his daughter Gloria Ann
summary: Baker reports that the 104-year-old Morton-Finney is still practicing law; Johnson recalls his fashionable daughter at Attucks.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: While we’re there, let me just ask you something about [something else]. We were talking last night. Was Dr. [John] Morton-Finney already at Attucks [Crispus Attucks High School in Indianapolis] when you were there?
My best recollection is that there was a Dr. Morton-Finney at Attucks.
He’s 104 years old now and still practicing law. I saw it in the Star [Indianapolis Star newspaper] yesterday.
That’s remarkable!
And fact is, [he] learned six languages. He just got a degree recently in something else.
What?
Yes, Dr. Morton-Finney.
One hundred and four? That’s fantastic!
And in good health.
Oh, that's –
They had a picture of him with a cigar and . . .
And still sharp.
He’s still taking cases.
What?
[laughs]
That is the most mind-blowing scenario I have ever heard of.

Lida asked me if he was there when you were there because, like I said, at one hundred and four he says he reads voraciously. He says he’s a biography nut. But I just wondered if he was your teacher like he was the rest of us.

That's remarkable. Well, you know, the name – I was telling Carolyn [Carolyn Johnson, J. J.'s wife] this just a few days ago. I don’t know how it came up between Carolyn and I about the name Morton-Finney. But in any case, I told her what I remember most about that name was [that his daughter] Gloria Ann Morton-Finney was a sharp, sharp dresser. She dressed to kill.
He lives with her. He lives with his daughter.
She’s still alive and he’s living with her now?
He lives with his daughter.
She was one of the sharpest dressers at Crispus Attucks. Gloria Ann Morton-Finney.
She was my substitute teacher. I remember her, too. Yes. I remember her well.
I remember her well, too. I remember because she was always such a fashion plate.
Yes.
[laughs]
